# A view generated by OCaml

Structured output can be visual without turning the document into an app
framework. This page samples two frequencies at 96 points—enough for a smooth
curve while keeping the complete execution inspectable—and asks OCaml to
generate one SVG path.

    let sample_count = 96
    let point index =
      let phase =
        float_of_int index /. float_of_int (sample_count - 1)
        *. 2. *. Float.pi
      in
      let x = 210. +. (175. *. sin (3. *. phase)) in
      let y = 105. +. (78. *. sin (4. *. phase +. 0.45)) in
      x, y
    let points =
      List.init sample_count point
      |> List.map (fun (x, y) ->
           Printf.sprintf "%.2f,%.2f" x y)
      |> String.concat " "

The SVG is emitted through `Doc.html`. It is rendered in a sandbox and stays
attached to this code block as the source changes.

    let view =
      {|
      <div class="card">
        <div class="eyebrow">3 : 4 frequency ratio</div>
        <svg viewBox="0 0 420 210" role="img"
             aria-label="A smooth Lissajous curve">
          <defs>
            <linearGradient id="ink" x1="0" x2="1">
              <stop stop-color="#285f4e"/>
              <stop offset="1" stop-color="#6e8692"/>
            </linearGradient>
          </defs>
          <polyline points="|}
      ^ points
      ^ {|"
            fill="none" stroke="url(#ink)" stroke-width="3"
            stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
        </svg>
      </div>
      <style>
        body { padding: 0; }
        .card {
          box-sizing: border-box;
          min-height: 240px;
          padding: 20px 22px 16px;
          border: 1px solid #e1e4df;
          border-radius: 12px;
          background:
            radial-gradient(circle at 50% 45%, #f4f7f4, #fffefa 68%);
        }
        .eyebrow {
          color: #758079;
          font: 600 11px/1.2 system-ui, sans-serif;
          letter-spacing: .08em;
          text-transform: uppercase;
        }
        svg { display: block; width: 100%; height: 200px; }
      </style>
      |}
    let () = Doc.html ~id:"lissajous" view

Try changing either frequency in `point`. The previous view fades immediately,
then the replacement appears when evaluation finishes.
